signature.instructions:
You are given the raw text of a political fundraising email (from a campaign committee, PAC, or party committee). Return the name of the political committee that SPONSORED / PAID FOR the email.

Where to look, in priority order:
1. The FEC disclaimer in the footer. It usually reads 'Paid for by <COMMITTEE NAME>', but it can also read 'Paid for and authorized by ...', 'Paid political advertisement paid for and provided in kind by ...', or 'Paid for and approved by ...'. Use the name exactly as it appears there.
2. If there is no disclaimer, use the committee name printed with the footer mailing address, or the organization soliciting the money (e.g. 'Contributions to <NAME> are not tax deductible', 'unsubscribe from <NAME>').

Rules for the output string:
- Output ONLY the committee name. Never include 'Paid for by', 'paid political advertisement', 'provided in kind by', 'and not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee', appended clauses such as 'a joint fundraising committee authorized by and composed of ...', street addresses, PO Boxes, city/state/ZIP, phone numbers, URLs, or trailing punctuation.
- REPRODUCE THE CASING EXACTLY AS PRINTED in the disclaimer. If the disclaimer is written in ALL CAPS, return the name in ALL CAPS; do NOT convert it to Title Case, and do not otherwise re-case, re-spell, abbreviate, or expand the name.
- Drop any parenthetical aside that follows the name, e.g. a website or acronym in parentheses such as '(SOMESITE.COM)'. The name ends where the '(' begins.
- The disclaimer is often NOT followed by punctuation: ordinary prose (a sentence about the candidate, an unsubscribe line, an address) can run straight into it. The committee name ends at the first ordinary lowercase word that is not a connector ('for', 'of', 'and', 'the', 'to'): words like 'is', 'was', 'has', 'who', 'this', 'contributions', 'unsubscribe' begin the next sentence and are NOT part of the name.
- Keep a person's middle initial together with its period (a single capital letter followed by a period is part of the name, NOT the end of a sentence). Likewise keep abbreviations such as 'Inc.', 'Jr.', 'U.S.' that belong to the name.
- Committee names often contain a NUMERAL used as wordplay, most commonly a single digit standing in for a word (a candidate name, then a lone digit, then a state or office). Keep such single digits: they are part of the name. In contrast, a number of TWO OR MORE digits right after the name is the start of the mailing address (street number, PO Box, ZIP, phone) and must be dropped along with everything after it.
- Email text often glues the committee name directly onto the following word, a web domain, or an email address with no space (e.g. a name immediately followed by 'www.<something>.org' or 'http...'). Cut everything from the domain/URL/@-address onward and return only the name part.
- Drop a leading article: return the bare committee name, not 'the <NAME>'.
- Line-wrap artifacts also glue two ordinary words together with no space (two names run together, a name glued to a small word such as 'for'/'of', or the disclaimer word glued to 'by', as in 'authorizedby'). Restore the missing space; elsewhere in the email the correctly spaced form usually appears, so use that spelling.
- Footers frequently print the committee name twice back-to-back (sometimes with the two copies glued together, sometimes with the second copy running into the next sentence); output it exactly once, in full.
- Never truncate the name early: give the COMPLETE name including every trailing 'for <office/state>' part.
- Give no explanation and no quotation marks.

module_src:
class IdentifyCommitteeModule(dspy.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        # The LLM is a LAST RESORT: used only when the deterministic parser cannot
        # recover a trustworthy committee name from the email text.
        self.fallback = dspy.Predict(dspy.Signature(
            "email_body: str -> committee: str",
            "You are given the raw text of a political fundraising email (from a campaign committee, PAC, "
            "or party committee). Return the name of the political committee that SPONSORED / PAID FOR "
            "the email.\n\n"
            "Where to look, in priority order:\n"
            "1. The FEC disclaimer in the footer. It usually reads 'Paid for by <COMMITTEE NAME>', but it "
            "can also read 'Paid for and authorized by ...', 'Paid political advertisement paid for and "
            "provided in kind by ...', or 'Paid for and approved by ...'. Use the name exactly as it "
            "appears there.\n"
            "2. If there is no disclaimer, use the committee name printed with the footer mailing address, "
            "or the organization soliciting the money (e.g. 'Contributions to <NAME> are not tax "
            "deductible', 'unsubscribe from <NAME>').\n\n"
            "Rules for the output string:\n"
            "- Output ONLY the committee name. Never include 'Paid for by', 'paid political "
            "advertisement', 'provided in kind by', 'and not authorized by any candidate or candidate's "
            "committee', appended clauses such as 'a joint fundraising committee authorized by and "
            "composed of ...', street addresses, PO Boxes, city/state/ZIP, phone numbers, URLs, or "
            "trailing punctuation.\n"
            "- REPRODUCE THE CASING EXACTLY AS PRINTED in the disclaimer. If the disclaimer is written in "
            "ALL CAPS, return the name in ALL CAPS; do NOT convert it to Title Case, and do not otherwise "
            "re-case, re-spell, abbreviate, or expand the name.\n"
            "- Drop any parenthetical aside that follows the name, e.g. a website or acronym in parentheses "
            "such as '(SOMESITE.COM)'. The name ends where the '(' begins.\n"
            "- The disclaimer is often NOT followed by punctuation: ordinary prose (a sentence about the "
            "candidate, an unsubscribe line, an address) can run straight into it. The committee name ends "
            "at the first ordinary lowercase word that is not a connector ('for', 'of', 'and', 'the', "
            "'to'): words like 'is', 'was', 'has', 'who', 'this', 'contributions', 'unsubscribe' begin the "
            "next sentence and are NOT part of the name.\n"
            "- Keep a person's middle initial together with its period (a single capital letter followed "
            "by a period is part of the name, NOT the end of a sentence). Likewise keep abbreviations such "
            "as 'Inc.', 'Jr.', 'U.S.' that belong to the name.\n"
            "- Committee names often contain a NUMERAL used as wordplay, most commonly a single digit "
            "standing in for a word (a candidate name, then a lone digit, then a state or office). Keep "
            "such single digits: they are part of the name. In contrast, a number of TWO OR MORE digits "
            "right after the name is the start of the mailing address (street number, PO Box, ZIP, "
            "phone) and must be dropped along with everything after it.\n"
            "- Email text often glues the committee name directly onto the following word, a web domain, "
            "or an email address with no space (e.g. a name immediately followed by 'www.<something>.org' "
            "or 'http...'). Cut everything from the domain/URL/@-address onward and return only the name "
            "part.\n"
            "- Drop a leading article: return the bare committee name, not 'the <NAME>'.\n"
            "- Line-wrap artifacts also glue two ordinary words together with no space (two names run "
            "together, a name glued to a small word such as 'for'/'of', or the disclaimer word glued to "
            "'by', as in 'authorizedby'). Restore the missing space; elsewhere in the email the correctly "
            "spaced form usually appears, so use that spelling.\n"
            "- Footers frequently print the committee name twice back-to-back (sometimes with the two "
            "copies glued together, sometimes with the second copy running into the next sentence); output "
            "it exactly once, in full.\n"
            "- Never truncate the name early: give the COMPLETE name including every trailing "
            "'for <office/state>' part.\n"
            "- Give no explanation and no quotation marks."
        ))

    def forward(self, **inputs):
        import re
        from collections import Counter

        body = inputs.get("email_body") or ""

        SMALL = {"for", "of", "the", "and", "a", "to", "in", "on", "at", "or"}
        # Lowercase words that may legitimately appear inside a committee name.
        PARTICLES = {"de", "del", "la", "le", "van", "von", "der", "den", "du", "di",
                     "da", "dos", "y", "e", "por", "con", "el", "al"}
        ALLOWED_LOWER = SMALL | PARTICLES
        NAME_PREFIXES = {"mc", "mac", "o", "de", "des", "di", "du", "la", "le", "van",
                         "von", "st", "el", "al", "d", "der", "den"}
        HARD_STOP = {"not", "po", "p.o.", "p.o", "pmb", "suite", "ste", "unsubscribe",
                     "paid", "copyright", "tel", "text", "contributions", "contribution",
                     "authorized", "www", "all", "privacy", "email", "sent", "click",
                     "donate", "box", "united", "address", "no", "if", "this", "via"}
        # Trailing-period tokens whose period belongs to the NAME, not a sentence end.
        ABBREV = {"inc", "llc", "jr", "sr", "st", "mt", "dr", "sen", "rep", "gov",
                  "cmte", "comm", "co", "ltd", "assn", "dept", "natl", "fnd"}
        KEYWORDS = {"for", "of", "committee", "friends", "fund", "pac", "victory",
                    "campaign", "team", "action", "majority", "project", "alliance",
                    "citizens", "americans"}

        # Matches an embedded URL / domain / mail-address start inside a token.
        URL_RE = re.compile(r"(?:https?:|www\.|\.(?:com|org|net|gov|edu|io|co|us|info)\b|@)", re.I)

        def normalize(t: str) -> str:
            """Collapse whitespace and strip invisible/odd characters from email text."""
            for ch in ("\u034f", "\u200b", "\u200c", "\u200d", "\ufeff", "\xa0", "\u00ad"):
                t = t.replace(ch, " ")
            t = t.replace("\u2019", "'").replace("\u2018", "'")
            t = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", t)
            return t.strip()

        text = normalize(body)

        # Frequency of every standalone alphabetic word in the email (lowercased).
        word_counts = Counter(w.lower() for w in re.findall(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z']*", text))

        def initial_or_abbrev(tok: str) -> bool:
            """True when a token's trailing period is part of the name.

            Covers middle initials ('B.'), dotted acronyms ('U.S.') and common
            name abbreviations ('Inc.', 'Jr.', 'St.'). Such a period must NOT be
            treated as the end of the disclaimer sentence.
            """
            if not tok.endswith("."):
                return False
            if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z](?:\.[A-Za-z])*\.", tok):
                return True
            return tok.rstrip(".").lower() in ABBREV

        def is_plain_lowercase_word(tok: str) -> bool:
            """True when the token is an ordinary all-lowercase word (prose, not a name part)."""
            core = tok.strip(".,;:!?'\"“”")
            if not core or not core.isalpha():
                return False
            return core.islower() and core.lower() not in ALLOWED_LOWER

        def split_glued(tok: str) -> list:
            """Split camel-case line-wrap glue ('EmiliaSykes' -> ['Emilia', 'Sykes']).

            Never splits all-caps tokens or right after a name particle (Mc, Mac, De, ...).
            """
            if tok.isupper() or len(tok) < 4:
                return [tok]
            parts = []
            start = 0
            for i in range(1, len(tok)):
                if tok[i].isupper() and tok[i - 1].islower():
                    left = tok[start:i]
                    if len(left) < 2 or left.lower() in NAME_PREFIXES:
                        continue
                    parts.append(left)
                    start = i
            parts.append(tok[start:])
            return [p for p in parts if p]

        def unglue(tok: str) -> list:
            """Split a lowercase-run / all-caps glue ('Rosenfor' -> ['Rosen', 'for'],
            'OFSHERROD' -> ['OF', 'SHERROD']).

            Only splits when the glued token is essentially unique in the email while
            BOTH halves occur elsewhere as standalone words, so ordinary words are safe.
            """
            if len(tok) < 7 or not tok.isalpha():
                return [tok]
            whole = word_counts.get(tok.lower(), 0)
            if whole > 2:
                return [tok]
            best = None
            for i in range(2, len(tok) - 1):
                left, right = tok[:i], tok[i:]
                if len(left) < 2 or len(right) < 2:
                    continue
                cl = word_counts.get(left.lower(), 0)
                cr = word_counts.get(right.lower(), 0)
                if cl < 1 or cr < 1:
                    continue
                if whole <= 1:
                    if min(cl, cr) < 1:
                        continue
                elif min(cl, cr) <= whole:
                    continue
                score = min(cl, cr)
                if best is None or score > best[0]:
                    best = (score, [left, right])
            return best[1] if best else [tok]

        def key_of(words: list) -> str:
            """Spacing/punctuation-insensitive key: lowercase alphanumerics only."""
            return "".join(c.lower() for w in words for c in w if c.isalnum())

        def dedupe_key(words: list) -> list:
            """Collapse a name printed twice back-to-back, ignoring spacing differences."""
            n = len(words)
            for k in range(1, n):
                first, second = words[:k], words[k:]
                a, b = key_of(first), key_of(second)
                if a and a == b:
                    return second if len(second) > len(first) else first
            return words

        def drop_trailing_repeat(words: list) -> list:
            """Drop a trailing block that simply repeats the block just before it.

            Footers often print '<NAME> <NAME> <prose...>' with no punctuation, so after
            truncating the prose we are left with the name twice, e.g.
            ['Friends','of','Katrina','Christiansen','Katrina','Christiansen'].
            """
            n = len(words)
            for m in range(n // 2, 0, -1):
                tail = key_of(words[n - m:])
                prev = key_of(words[n - 2 * m:n - m])
                if tail and tail == prev:
                    return words[:n - m]
            return words

        def cut_at_url(tok: str):
            """Return the name-part of a token that has a URL / domain / email glued on.

            'Projectwww.protectvoting.org' -> 'Project';  'www.NRSC.org' -> ''.
            Returns None when the token contains no URL-like fragment.
            """
            m = URL_RE.search(tok)
            if not m:
                return None
            return tok[:m.start()].strip(".,;:!'\"()[]")

        def digit_break(core: str) -> bool:
            """True when a token beginning with a digit ENDS the committee name.

            A lone single digit inside a name is wordplay for a word ('<Name> 4 <State>')
            and must be kept. A run of two or more digits is a street number, PO Box,
            ZIP or phone number, i.e. the start of the address block.
            """
            m = re.match(r"\d+", core)
            if not m:
                return False
            return len(m.group(0)) > 1

        def tokens_after_disclaimer(rest: str) -> list:
            """Collect the committee-name tokens that follow a 'paid for ... by' marker."""
            toks = rest.split(" ")[:30]
            kept = []
            for j, raw in enumerate(toks):
                tok = raw.strip("*|›‹>«»•·—–_\"“”…")
                if not tok:
                    break
                # A parenthetical aside (website/acronym) terminates the name.
                if tok[:1] in "([{":
                    break
                mp = re.search(r"[\(\[\{]", tok)
                if mp:
                    head = tok[:mp.start()].strip(".,;:!'\"")
                    if head and head.lower() not in HARD_STOP:
                        kept.append(head)
                    break
                core_num = tok.strip(".,;:!'\"")
                if core_num[:1].isdigit() and digit_break(core_num):
                    break
                # A glued URL / domain / email address terminates the name.
                cut = cut_at_url(tok)
                if cut is not None:
                    if cut and cut.lower() not in HARD_STOP:
                        kept.append(cut)
                    break
                low = tok.lower().strip(".,;:!'")
                if low in HARD_STOP or not low:
                    break
                # Ordinary lowercase prose word => the disclaimer sentence is over.
                if j > 0 and is_plain_lowercase_word(tok):
                    break
                if low in ("and", "is", "but", "&"):
                    nxt = toks[j + 1].lower() if j + 1 < len(toks) else ""
                    if nxt.startswith("not") or nxt.startswith("is") or nxt.startswith("author"):
                        break
                if tok[-1] in ".,;:!":
                    if tok[-1] == "." and initial_or_abbrev(tok):
                        kept.append(tok)          # middle initial / abbreviation: keep going
                        if len(kept) >= 20:
                            break
                        continue
                    inner = tok.rstrip(".,;:!")
                    if inner:
                        kept.append(inner)
                    break
                kept.append(tok)
                if len(kept) >= 20:
                    break
            return kept

        def polish(kept: list) -> str:
            words = []
            for tok in kept:
                for part in split_glued(tok):
                    words.extend(unglue(part))
            for _ in range(3):
                new = dedupe_key(words)
                if new == words:
                    break
                words = new
            for _ in range(3):
                new = drop_trailing_repeat(words)
                if new == words:
                    break
                words = new
            if not words:
                return ""
            all_caps = all(c.isupper() for c in "".join(words) if c.isalpha())
            # Drop a leading article ('the NRCC' -> 'NRCC'); keep an intentional 'The'.
            while len(words) > 1 and words[0].lower() == "the" and (words[0].islower() or all_caps):
                words.pop(0)
            # Trim trailing filler: small words and dangling numerals.
            while words and (words[-1].lower() in ALLOWED_LOWER or words[-1].isdigit()):
                words.pop()
            while words and not any(c.isalnum() for c in words[0]):
                words.pop(0)
            if not words:
                return ""
            # Casing is preserved exactly as printed in the email (ALL CAPS stays ALL CAPS).
            return " ".join(words).strip(" .,;:-")

        def suspicious(cand: str) -> bool:
            """True when the extracted name is probably corrupted/truncated -> defer."""
            toks = cand.split()
            if not toks or len(toks) > 9:
                return True
            k = key_of(toks)
            if len(k) < 3:
                return True
            n = len(k)
            if n % 2 == 0 and k[: n // 2] == k[n // 2:]:
                return True  # name still doubled
            if not any(t[:1].isupper() for t in toks):
                return True  # no capitalized word: unlikely to be a proper name
            if URL_RE.search(cand):
                return True  # leftover URL / domain / email debris
            if re.search(r"[A-Za-z]\.[A-Za-z]{3,}", cand):
                return True
            if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z]\.?", toks[-1]):
                return True  # truncated right at a middle initial
            if len(toks) == 1 and not (toks[0].isupper() or any(c.isdigit() for c in toks[0])):
                return True  # a bare single word is almost never a full committee name
            for i, t in enumerate(toks):
                if i > 0 and is_plain_lowercase_word(t):
                    return True  # ordinary prose word leaked into the name
                if len(t) >= 12 and t.isalpha() and t[1:].islower() \
                        and word_counts.get(t.lower(), 0) <= 1:
                    return True  # long unique lowercase-run token: unresolved glue
            return False

        def deterministic(t: str) -> str:
            """Extract the sponsoring committee from the FEC 'paid for ... by' disclaimer(s)."""
            candidates = []
            # Covers 'paid for by', 'paid for and authorized by', 'paid for and approved by',
            # 'paid for and provided in kind by', and line-wrap glue like 'authorizedby'.
            patterns = [
                r"paid\s*for\s*(?:and\s*(?:\w+\s*){0,3}?)?by",
                r"provided\s+in\s+kind\s*by",
                r"authorized\s+and\s+paid\s*for\s*by",
            ]
            for pattern in patterns:
                for m in re.finditer(pattern, t, re.I):
                    nxt = t[m.end():m.end() + 1]
                    # 'by' swallowed inside a longer word (e.g. 'bystander'): not a marker.
                    if nxt and nxt.isalpha() and nxt.islower():
                        continue
                    rest = t[m.end():].lstrip(" :,-–—.")
                    if not rest:
                        continue
                    cand = polish(tokens_after_disclaimer(rest))
                    if not cand:
                        continue
                    n_words = len(cand.split())
                    if n_words < 1 or n_words > 9:
                        continue
                    if not any(c.isalpha() for c in cand) or len(cand) < 3:
                        continue
                    if cand.lower() in ("the", "a", "an", "any", "our", "this"):
                        continue
                    candidates.append(cand)
                if candidates:
                    break  # prefer the highest-priority disclaimer wording found
            if not candidates:
                return ""
            keys = [key_of(c.split()) for c in candidates]
            counts = Counter(keys)
            best_n = max(counts.values())
            best_key = None
            for kk in keys:
                if counts[kk] == best_n:
                    best_key = kk
                    break
            group = [c for c, kk in zip(candidates, keys) if kk == best_key]
            group.sort(key=lambda c: -len(c.split()))
            return group[0]

        def address_candidate(t: str) -> str:
            """Recover the committee name printed right before the footer mailing address.

            Deliberately conservative: the phrase must look committee-like (contain a word
            such as 'for', 'committee', 'friends', 'fund', 'PAC') AND occur at least twice
            in the email, otherwise we leave the email to the LLM rather than guess.
            """
            text_key = "".join(c.lower() for c in t if c.isalnum())
            best = ""
            addr_re = re.compile(r"(?:\bP\.?\s?O\.?\s+Box\b|\b\d{2,6}\s+[A-Z][a-z])")
            for m in addr_re.finditer(t):
                prefix = t[:m.start()].rstrip(" ,.-–—")
                toks = prefix.split(" ")[-14:]
                acc = []
                for raw in reversed(toks):
                    tok = raw.strip("*|›‹>«»•·—–_[]()\"“”…")
                    if not tok:
                        break
                    if URL_RE.search(tok):
                        break
                    low = tok.lower().strip(".,;:!'")
                    if not low or low in HARD_STOP:
                        break
                    if tok[-1] in ".,;:!?" and not initial_or_abbrev(tok):
                        break
                    core = tok.strip(".,;:!'\"")
                    if core[:1].isdigit() and digit_break(core):
                        break
                    if not (tok[:1].isupper() or low in ALLOWED_LOWER or core.isdigit()):
                        break
                    acc.append(tok)
                    if len(acc) >= 10:
                        break
                cand = polish(list(reversed(acc)))
                if not cand:
                    continue
                parts = cand.split()
                if len(parts) < 2:
                    continue
                if not any(w.lower().strip(".,;:'") in KEYWORDS for w in parts):
                    continue
                k = key_of(parts)
                if len(k) < 6 or text_key.count(k) < 2:
                    continue
                if len(cand) > len(best):
                    best = cand
            return best

        committee = deterministic(text)

        if not committee or suspicious(committee):
            alt = address_candidate(text)
            if alt and not suspicious(alt):
                committee = alt
            else:
                out = self.fallback(email_body=body)
                guess = str(getattr(out, "committee", "") or "").strip().strip('"“”')
                guess = re.sub(r"^\s*paid\s+for\s+(?:and\s+(?:\w+\s+){0,4}?)?by\s+", "",
                               guess, flags=re.I).strip(" .,;:-")
                guess = re.sub(r"^the\s+(?=[A-Z])", "", guess).strip(" .,;:-")
                # Strip a parenthetical aside the LLM may have carried over.
                pm = re.search(r"[\(\[]", guess)
                if pm and guess[: pm.start()].strip(" .,;:-"):
                    guess = guess[: pm.start()].strip(" .,;:-")
                # Strip any URL / email debris the LLM may have carried over.
                m = URL_RE.search(guess)
                if m and guess[: m.start()].strip(" .,;:-"):
                    guess = guess[: m.start()].strip(" .,;:-")
                if guess:
                    committee = guess

        return dspy.Prediction(committee=str(committee).strip())
